ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small block with a charge of $+q$ and mass $\mathbf{m}$ is placed on a smooth inclined plane with an angle of $37^{\circ}$. When the entire setup is placed in a uniform electric field directed horizontally to the right, the small block remains stationary. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$, and $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$.

1. Find the magnitude of the electric field strength directed horizontally to the right.
2. If the electric field strength is changed to be vertically downward with the same magnitude, find the magnitude of the acceleration of the small block when it is released from rest at a height H.
3. If the electric field strength is changed to be vertically downward with the same magnitude, find the speed of the small block when it is released from rest at height $H$ and reaches the ground.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small block with a charge of $+q$ and mass $\mathbf{m}$ is placed on a smooth inclined plane with an angle of $37^{\circ}$. When the entire setup is placed in a uniform electric field directed horizontally to the right, the small block remains stationary. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$, and $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$. 1. Find the magnitude of the electric field strength directed horizontally to the right. 2. If the electric field strength is changed to be vertically downward with the same magnitude, find the magnitude of the acceleration of the small block when it is released from rest at a height H. 3. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a smooth inclined plane slanting from the lower left to the upper right, with an inclination angle of 37° marked at the bottom; a small block is located on the inclined plane. Multiple horizontal arrows in the figure all point to the right and are labeled E, indicating that the uniform electric field is horizontally to the right. The small block is positively charged, so the direction of the electric field force is the same as the direction of the electric field, horizontally to the right. Reasoning: When the electric field is horizontally to the right, the small block is subjected to gravity mg vertically downward, the electric field force qE horizontally to the right, and the support force of the inclined plane on it perpendicular to the inclined plane. Decompose along the direction of the inclined plane: the component of the electric field force upward along the inclined plane is qE cos37°, and the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sin37°. The small block is at rest, so qE cos37° = mg sin37°. Therefore E = mg sin37°/(q cos37°) = mg tan37°/q = mg*(0.6/0.8)/q = 3mg/(4q). When the electric field is changed to vertically downward and its magnitude remains unchanged, the electric field force qE on the positive charge is also vertically downward, with magnitude qE = q·3mg/(4q) = 3mg/4. Thus the equivalent total force vertically downward is mg + qE = mg + 3mg/4 = 7mg/4. Its component downward along the inclined plane is (7mg/4)sin37° = (7mg/4)*0.6 = 21mg/20, so the acceleration a = (21mg/20)/m = 21g/20. If it is released from rest at a vertical height H from the ground, when it reaches the ground the displacement along the inclined plane is s = H/sin37° = H/0.6. Using v^2 = 2as, obtain v^2 = 2*(21g/20)*(H/0.6) = 7gH/2. Therefore v = sqrt(7gH/2) = sqrt(14gH)/2.
